target_customer: Industrial biotech and specialty chemical firms that want microbes engineered to make a target molecule
problem: Designing a microbe to produce a specific chemical was slow and manual. 20n sold software that predicts the biochemistry and designs the organism for a named target molecule.
business_model: software-designed microbe licenses (reported to start in the hundreds of thousands of dollars) plus DARPA-supported research

founders.name: Saurabh Srivastava
education: PhD in computer science (institution not named by sources)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch Feb 2015 and the YC page say he has a PhD in computer science and worked with a DARPA-backed Berkeley lab.

founders.name: J. Christopher Anderson
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch describes 17 years of synthetic biology experience. YC lists him as Chris Anderson.

technical_complexity.rationale: Predicting enzyme pathways and organism designs from biological data was research-grade work in 2015, built on program synthesis and data mining by two people.

defensibility.rationale: The approach rested on specialised algorithms and an academic lab pipeline. Customers still needed wet-lab validation and rivals such as large synthetic biology firms had their own tools.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source reports any incumbent copying or buying 20n. Sources conflict on whether the company still operates.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (Feb 2015) reports the founders pitching specialty chemicals as a very large market and said they were negotiating several licensing contracts, which suggests early customer interest, though no revenue figure is given.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, brand page or community evidence about the name or identity was found. The name was later reused by an unrelated company, 20n Bio, which makes it confusable in searches.

outcome_analysis: 20n launched from a DARPA-backed UC Berkeley lab with a software platform that designs microbes for target chemicals, and had early licensing talks in early 2015. The YC directory lists it as inactive, while other databases still show it as active or alive, and no shutdown cause is public, so no failure factors are assigned. Funding is only partly known from database entries.
notes: Company website 20n.com could not be fetched (DNS failure in the session network), so it is not confirmed dead. Status conflict: YC and one startup map say inactive or closed; CB Insights lists Seed, Alive and Craft lists Active. Funding conflict: CB Insights total of about $120K (the YC deal), Craft total $2.2M, iAmsterdam map $2.1M seed, StartupIntros seed of $2M. The seed round rests on single databases and an unopened StartupIntros listing; investors are unknown. DARPA support is stated on the YC page but no grant amount was found. The competitor search found only general synthetic biology articles (Zymergen, Ginkgo, Amyris, Genomatica) dated after the batch or undated, and the TechCrunch launch article names no rivals, so the list is empty. Do not confuse with 20n Bio (2021, Malvern PA).
